C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2.Summary: Stop tests from invoking a mutating record operation against the real repository tree. Relocate the second --retire writes-no-byte probe onto an isolated fixture so the coverage survives. Flush the four staged findings F192 F193 F194 F195 into the live record with index entries, mint the live chartered registry row for this bundle, and correct every sentence in the retired C-CODIFY-DECISIONS registry row which a bundle has falsified. The charter row pays F192, F194, F195 and deliberately not F193. Binding live rulings D11, D27, D28, D28.1, D30. This bundle writes the record; D30 is scoped, not skirted. The flush and charter membership assertions are invariant under this bundle's own close, so the suite stays green after archive. The shipped F21 live-pair assertion is reshaped to the same invariant form in this bundle.
C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2.Problem:
A test performs a governed record operation against the production record.
scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts main() treats --retire as the move: retireRecord with repoRoot equal to cwd (:1431-1434). retireRecord returns without writing when movedCount is 0 (:1044-1047). When anything is eligible it stamps, moves, rewrites every live root, and writes the retired siblings (:1119-1125). Eligibility is the enforcement (D28.1): a finding whose PaidBy names an archived bundle (:988-1000, validated :1209-1215); a decision whose CodifiedIn children all resolve (:1015-1018, validated :1260-1265); a live registry row whose name equals an archive directory (:1030-1036, validated :1230-1234). A resolving TaughtIn is not eligibility.
scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts invokes that move against REPO_ROOT at two sites (:1466 AC-PAYMENT-SET, :1525 AC-TAG-AND-RETIRE): snapshot production files, runValidator(REPO_ROOT, ["--retire"]), assert byte-identity. That assertion holds only while nothing is eligible. The moment something is, the test performs the retirement, then fails the byte comparison on a tree it already mutated.
Closing a bundle archives it, which makes its own live charter row eligible, and close ceremony then re-runs the suite. Every bundle that mints a charter row reproduces the condition, including this one.
The originating ruling is not the production invocation. C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY required a second --retire with nothing eligible to be a no-op that does not rewrite ceiling (.ngrace/changes/archive/C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY/spec.xml:349-351) and required production validate with no mutating argv never to write (:358-359). T-004 already implements that no-op on isolatedRoot (validate-record-retirement.test.ts:1131-1154). AC-PAYMENT-SET required a production read plus validate exit 0. AC-TAG-AND-RETIRE required bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts with no mutating argv. The production --retire calls exceed those criteria. This spec does not overturn the no-op ruling. It relocates the extra production invocation that violates (a).
How this bundle exists. Its substance is the approved spec of C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION, ratified twice, whose archived copy stands at .ngrace/changes/archive/C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION/spec.xml. The bundle was superseded for its plan, not this spec's substance: the ratified plan contradicted itself on the close boundary — its IntentSummary listed terminal and fold among the cursor events execution emits, then forbade both as close acts three lines later, while the two per-task copies carried only the forbidding form. D27 rules that an approved governance artifact is repaired by ngrace supersede and a replacement bundle, and that amend-and-re-ratify is not available, so the whole bundle was archived under <Replacement>C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2</Replacement>. This spec carries that approved substance forward under the new name with the bundle's identity sentences rewritten and every measured figure re-derived at the current commit (Assumptions); the archived bundle is immutable and nothing in it is edited.
The criteria in this spec assert properties invariant under this bundle's own close — archive then --retire moves the charter row and the findings it pays — and the payment is explicit. That shape is not decoration: closing a bundle archives it, which makes its own live charter row eligible, and close ceremony re-runs the suite, so a criterion asserting live membership begins to falsify at exactly the close it is supposed to pass. Both directions verified on a throwaway fixture driven through the real validator (Assumptions).
The carve-out ground was then checked against each assertion it covers. The ground holds for every retired-side assertion and fails for exactly one: the F21 live pair, which has never moved and carries no payer today, so the same scheduled-payment argument the Constraint itself makes falsifies it — this bundle reshapes it (AC-DUPLICATE-PAIR) instead of exempting it. The sibling split-token sentence was probed and is false in the current product: no shipped validator refuses a token split across a live file and its retired sibling; the slug-grammar mechanism F172 described was removed with the markdown genres (commit 67bc55c).

Goals.Goal: Isolation. No test in this repository invokes --retire, --stamp-paid-by, or --split against the real repository tree. runValidator(REPO_ROOT, mutating argv) is gone. Operator --retire against production remains the shipped command; the validator must not refuse cwd equal to the repository root.

The probe survives on an isolated fixture. A --retire with nothing eligible remains a byte-identical no-op (T-004 stays). A second --retire after a successful move on a fixture writes no byte. Those assertions run with cwd equal to isolatedRoot, never REPO_ROOT. Production tests keep a read of the real record and a non-mutating validate.

Duplicate pairs. The shipped F21 pair assertion (validate-record-retirement.test.ts:1453-1454) stops requiring a named Finding to live in findings.xml. This bundle reshapes it to the move-invariant pair form (AC-DUPLICATE-PAIR): a duplicate-token pair is handled as a pair, whatever layer a lawful later payment gives it. The settled retired-side assertions keep their settled ground and are not rewritten (Constraint).

Flush. The four staged findings F192, F193, F194, F195 in .ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md land as live Finding elements in findings.xml and as index Entry elements in decisions.xml, layer live. Cut each body at the --- or ## STAGED CHARTER boundary first; a staged charter row is not an entry. There is no staged charter in the current buffer (Assumptions).

Charter row. Mint a live kind="chartered" Row name="C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2" in registry.xml, with the mint search in the house form in its Charter. Its location is the record's own move: live in registry.xml until this bundle archives, then retired by the close's --retire; the criteria assert its presence invariantly, not its layer.
Payment, carried from the superseded bundle's approved spec. The row carries a Pays element naming exactly F192, F194, F195. Evidence: the fix settles F195 — its two production mutating sites are the defect; the sweep settles F194 outright, whose owner is the next chartered bundle by that finding's own record, and this is that bundle; and the sweep completes F192, whose two original phrases T-003 already corrected and whose remaining falsified copies the whole-row re-read removes. F193 is deliberately absent: recorded, not paid; the window clamp is a later bundle's product change. A live row's name is not an archive directory, so the payment matures only at this bundle's close.

Sweep. Correct every sentence in the C-CODIFY-DECISIONS row in registry-retired.xml which a bundle has falsified, discovered by checking that row's claims against the current code and record. Not an enumerated phrase list. The spec-time audit in Assumptions is the floor, not the ceiling: implementation re-reads the whole row and corrects every falsified sentence it finds.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T2 (cross-cutting): the retirement test file and the record files this bundle writes. No graph module is written. Not T3: no new product subsystem, no lint-domain expansion, the record is not added to the artifact grammar, and src/ is not edited. Gates still run. Roadmap RM-GOVERNED-PATH. Binding live rulings: D11, D27, D28, D28.1, D30.

Remedy choice, normative. Isolated fixture, not an eligibility pre-check that still invokes --retire on production, and not dropping the no-op assertion. The pre-check still invokes a mutating operation against the real tree, which Goal (a) forbids, and a false-negative check would still mutate. Dropping --retire from the assertion without relocating it would overturn C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY's no-op criterion (archive spec.xml:349-351) and C-CODIFY-DECISIONS's byte-identical no-op Constraint; that is a regression dressed as a fix, and this spec does not overturn those rulings. Relocating onto isolatedRoot keeps the probe and satisfies (a). Production observation of nothing-eligible stays as non-mutating validate, which already errors finding-eligible-still-live, decision-eligible-still-live, and registry-eligible-still-live. Discrimination, required of the later plan: (1) T-004 remains red if retireRecord writes when movedCount is 0 (the early return at :1044-1047 deleted or persistSnapshot run anyway). (2) A fixture with an eligible entry: first --retire writes, second --retire is byte-identical; if the second wrote, the assertion fails. (3) The argv-fixture test still proves a fixture --retire does not read or write the repository record files. (4) A regression in the test file fails if any runValidator(REPO_ROOT, ...) args include --retire, --stamp-paid-by, or --split. Do not add a validator-side refuse of production cwd: the operator command must still move the real record.

This bundle writes the record, and D30 is scoped not skirted. The writes are: the four Finding elements and matching decisions.xml Entry elements; one live kind="chartered" Row in registry.xml; corrections inside the existing C-CODIFY-DECISIONS Row in registry-retired.xml; and whatever live-root attribute rewrite keeps base / headroom consistent with the shipped formulas after those appends. Ceiling attributes are rewritten only by --retire and never raised; a flush that would exceed a persisted ceiling stops and reports, it does not raise. Do not pin a scalar count of a record file into this Constraint; occupancy is in Assumptions. The freeze holds for the execution window that reads or rewrites the record files. Findings raised during that window go to the staged buffer, not into the record under edit.

Sweep rule, not a phrase list. The retired C-CODIFY-DECISIONS row is in registry-retired.xml. Correct every sentence in that row which a bundle has falsified. Discover the population by reading the whole row against the current validator, the current live and retired record, and the archived C-CODIFY-DECISIONS spec. The Assumptions audit is what this spec found at its writing commit; it is not a closed list. A claim written twice is corrected in every copy this row still carries. Do not re-introduce sentences T-003 already removed. The retired layer has no ceiling attributes (verified in Assumptions); this write costs no live window. --retire selects by token, not id, so every live element sharing a token moves together in one pass; before any insert confirm the tokens are absent from the live and retired siblings. A duplicate token split across a live file and its retired sibling is refused by no shipped validator — probed at this commit, all three exit 0 on such a fixture (Assumptions); the earlier citation-validator-red claim rested on the markdown-era slug grammar that commit 67bc55c removed, and this bundle does not rely on it. Do not mint a Decision. StatusText "Position pending the maintainer's word" stays unless a later audit finds a maintainer position that C-CODIFY-DECISIONS's NonGoal said not to write.

The four entries are F192, F193, F194, F195, each with its delimiter- preserving id (f192, f193, f194, f195). Write <Finding id="…" token="…" status="live"> with Title and Body from those entries, and <Entry id="…" token="…" genre="finding" layer="live" /> in decisions.xml. Confirm those tokens are absent from live and retired findings before insert. F193 is recorded, not paid: this bundle does not change the window clamp F193 names. After the flush, prune the four entries from the staged buffer only as the buffer's own header already instructs (after the flush PR merges, never before); this spec does not require a tracked write of that gitignored file.

Write scope, anchors, and imports. Files this spec forces into write scope, LINKS headers checked: scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts (no LINKS header; scripts/ is in .ngrace-lint.json ignoredDirs; M-RELEASE-AUTOMATION is not in .ngrace/graph and remains deferred), and the record files this bundle writes: docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml, decisions.xml, registry.xml, registry-retired.xml, plus the bundle's own artifacts. Do not edit scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts unless a test-only change is impossible; the operator --retire path stays. No graph module is written; do not mint a synthetic module. Do not add a ngrace lint issue code. Do not register the record files in CONTEXT_ARTIFACTS. AffectedAreas does not repeat this list (F136.1).

Tests do not pin a mutable production value of the record genres: neither a scalar count of live findings, live Decision elements, live registry rows, or any live-root occupancy, nor a membership or location claim — a test must not require a named Finding, Decision, or Row to live in one specific genre file when a scheduled payment can lawfully move it (registry rows move at their bundle's close; findings move when a payer names them). A production test that locates an entry asserts a property invariant under the retirement move — the entry occurs exactly once across the live file and its retired sibling, never in both, never in neither, with the decisions.xml index layer agreeing with the file that holds it — or pins content the move cannot rewrite: the retired layer, which retireRecord only appends to. The carve-out that stays legitimate is the settled ground, and only the assertions resting on it: the shipped AC-PAYMENT-SET assertions on the four historical registry rows, the seven paid tokens, and the F27.1 retired pair, and the shipped AC-TAG-AND-RETIRE assertions on D5.1, D7, D9, D18, and D24, all assert retired-layer content of entries that have already moved. retireRecord re-scans only live files, skips rows already retired (:1031-1032), appends to retired siblings without rewriting them (:1049-1074), and never returns an entry to live, so no lawful future move falsifies those assertions — a later payment cannot move an already-moved entry, the live-side absence clauses rest on the same one-directional ground, and what could falsify them is a hand edit of retired content, which the archive-immutability Constraint refuses. The F21 pair assertion (:1453-1454) does not rest on that ground and is not exempt: F21 has never moved and no payer names it today, so a scheduled payment can lawfully move it — this bundle reshapes it to the move-invariant pair form in AC-DUPLICATE-PAIR instead of leaving it live-pinned. This spec's prose contains no sentence matching the phrase that derivePayerMap's archived-spec pass keys on, so the archived copy cannot mint payments by prose. Fixture snapshots carry their own numbers. A --retire with nothing eligible remains a byte-identical no-op and must not rewrite any attribute.

Archive immutability. Do not edit anything under docs/plans/archive/ or tracked paths under .ngrace/changes/archive/ except this bundle's own later arrival there. Do not restamp D24. Do not rewrite retired findings or rulings bodies.

Evidence hygiene, settled lessons. Every diff-based criterion's command scopes to exactly the paths its prose names; prose and pathspec are the same set. A CloseEvidence pathspec covering a bundle-bearing directory excludes this bundle's own path, including in the post-close state. Archive-protection prose says tracked paths. Every task Verification command the later plan records must exit 0 as written at recording time. --run-commands needs an open cursor on a declared task and exiting 1 before execution is not a defect. Task Verification and TargetAssertions contain no current-mode lint of this project root — the rule: the command text contains --assertions current, or it invokes ngrace lint of this root and omits --assertions; checked by hand because the shipped detector misses bun ./src/grace.ts lint (F171). Current-mode lint appears only as post-archive AC-CLOSE-LINT. The later plan emits its own execution-time cursor events; do not omit them.

C-REPORT-HONESTY stands. Do not silence current-mode baseline issues, do not infer writes-started from git dirty, the ledger, or ObservedWriteScope, and do not treat bun test green as the evidence — the ExpectedEvidence probes are discriminating fixtures run against the delivered product.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-NO-PRODUCTION-MUTATION:
No test invokes --retire, --stamp-paid-by, or --split with cwd equal to the real repository root. The two sites runValidator(REPO_ROOT, ["--retire"]) at scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:1466 and :1525 are gone. AC-PAYMENT-SET and AC-TAG-AND-RETIRE still read the production record and still run non-mutating validate against REPO_ROOT. Failure: any test spawn of validate-record-retirement.ts with a mutating flag and cwd REPO_ROOT; or a write into docs/plans/active/, .ngrace/changes/, or the record files at the real repository root from a test.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PROBE-RELOCATED:
A --retire with nothing eligible on isolatedRoot leaves every planted record file byte-identical (T-004). A fixture with something eligible: first --retire writes, second --retire writes no byte, and the repository record files are unchanged. Failure: the no-op path writes; the second --retire after a move writes; either path writes the real tree.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DUPLICATE-PAIR:
The shipped F21 pair assertion (validate-record-retirement.test.ts:1453-1454, added at implementation by C-PAYMENT-RECORD, commit 3b64a12, absent from that archived spec's AC-PAYMENT-SET) stops asserting where F21 lives and asserts that the duplicate-token pair is handled as a pair, invariant under the retirement move. Over token F21's elements f21 and f21-correction: each id occurs exactly once across findings.xml and findings-retired.xml — never in both files, never in neither, never duplicated within one file — both ids occur in the same one of the two files, and decisions.xml carries exactly one Entry element per id whose layer agrees with the file holding the Finding. No status, layer, or PaidBy of F21 is pinned: a lawful future payment moves the pair together and the invariant holds in either layer (probed both directions on a fixture, Assumptions). The move cannot split the pair — the finding scan keys the payer on the token (validate-record-retirement.ts:988-1000), so every live element sharing it takes the same payer in the same pass — and that is the property the reshaped assertion keeps proving. The retired-side pair assertion (F27.1, :1441-1442) is untouched: it rests on retired-layer content. Failure: an id absent from both files (an element was lost); an id present in both (a copy, not a move); the two ids in different files (a select-by-id regression split the pair); an index Entry whose layer contradicts the Finding's file. The retirement test file reads the real record for this pair and carries an explicit generous timeout.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FLUSH:
After apply, each of F192, F193, F194, F195 exists as exactly one Finding element across findings.xml and findings-retired.xml — present in one of the two, never in both, never in neither — and decisions.xml carries exactly one matching Entry element genre="finding" whose layer agrees with the file that holds the Finding (live with findings.xml, retired with findings-retired.xml). A retired copy of a paid token (F192, F194, F195) carries PaidBy C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2. F193 is asserted present, not located: this bundle does not pay it, so it is live until a later bundle pays it, and the criterion must survive that move too. bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts (no mutating argv) exits 0 pre-archive and post-close; between the archive git mv and the close's --retire it exits 1 on registry-eligible-still-live and finding-eligible-still-live, which is the eligibility enforcement (D28.1), not a defect. Failure: a token absent from both files (the flush never happened); a token in both files (a copy, not a move); an index Entry whose layer contradicts the Finding's file; a retired paid token whose PaidBy does not name this bundle. The retirement test file reads the real record for these tokens and carries an explicit generous timeout.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CHARTER:
Exactly one of registry.xml and registry-retired.xml holds a kind="chartered" Row name="C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2" — never both, never neither — whose Charter records the mint search in the house form, and whose derived payment set (the F-tokens in its Pays plus any Closed-with tokens in its StatusText) is exactly F192, F194, F195. F193 appears nowhere in the row's Pays, and no Closed-with sentence in its StatusText names an F-token. The archive-collision case is enforced at mint time — refuseExistingBundle refuses an existing active or archive directory (src/grace-generate.ts) and the mint search in Assumptions measured zero archive, live, or retired rows for the exact name — not by this criterion: after this bundle archives, the archive directory with this name is this bundle's own arrival, not a collision. The retirement test file reads the real registry for this name and carries an explicit generous timeout. Failure: no row in either file (the charter never minted); the row in both files; a derived payment set other than exactly F192, F194, F195; a Charter without the mint search.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SWEEP:
Every sentence in the C-CODIFY-DECISIONS row in registry-retired.xml which a bundle has falsified is corrected, including every copy of a claim written twice. Implementation re-reads the whole row against current code and record; the Assumptions population is not a closed list. The row stays status="retired" kind="chartered". Failure: a sentence the current code falsifies still stands; a T-003 correction is reverted; the row moves live. The retirement test file reads that retired row and carries an explicit generous timeout. This criterion carries no close-coupled membership: its assertions attach to retired-layer content, which the close cannot rewrite — retireRecord only appends to registry-retired.xml — so it holds unchanged in the post-close state (Assumptions probe). The assertions must scope to the C-CODIFY-DECISIONS row itself, never to whole-file properties of registry-retired.xml, which the close grows by one row.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
